title: Seven Deadly Fitness Sins: Envy
summary: In his capital sins of fitness series he treats envy as a useful driving force that turns toxic when it becomes jealousy. He criticises tribal hate between bodybuilders and powerlifters and says the cure is putting in the work.
claims: Taking inspiration from physiques like Arnold's is healthy, but it should never turn into adoration or subservience
Do not try to become someone else; strive to become your own person
Living vicariously through someone else's body or strength is a waste of life; he would rather you train for five minutes than watch one of his five-minute videos
Envy can be a lifelong driving force that keeps pushing you forward, like lust
Envy becomes a sin when it turns into jealousy and resentment toward the people who have what you want
YouTube fitness is full of jealousy, with bodybuilders calling powerlifters fat and powerlifters calling bodybuilders weak pretty boys; real lifters do not partake
Lifters should support each other even when pursuing different goals
The easiest way to avoid jealousy is to put in the work; the most jealous people he has met only talk and never act
Hate aimed at someone who does not know you exist would make you far happier if spent lifting
